newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian foreign minister wins party post.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian foreign minister wins party post.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi on Thursday won one of the three vice presidential seats in triennial elections of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's political party.
Abdullah, a staunch ally of the prime minister, got 1,053 votes to unseat Youth and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin in the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) polls.
Education Minister Najib Tun Razak and Chief Minister of central Selangor state Muhammad Muhammad Taib polled 1,483 votes and 1,045 votes, respectively, to retain their vice presidencies in UMNO.
UMNO is the main political party in the ruling National Front coalition, which has ruled Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.
Mahathir and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim were not challenged in the elections, viewed as more significant than a general election, which the National Front has always won easily.
By political convention, the president and deputy president of UMNO serve as prime minister and deputy prime minister.
Badawi lost the vice presidency in 1993 when a team led by Muhyiddin and aligned to Anwar swept the top jobs.
